title: GOP gov candidate recounts miracle water landing as dispatch audio reveals desperate search for sinking plane
summary: Dispatch audio captures the frantic search for Tom Tiffany after his plane lost power and plunged into Lake Wausau in darkness Saturday night.
story: Dispatch audio captures the frantic search for Wisconsin GOP gubernatorial candidate Tom Tiffany and his pilot after their plane lost power and sank in Lake Wausau. (Audio provided by Broadcastify)

A desperate search unfolded across a dark Wisconsin lake after Republican gubernatorial candidate Tom Tiffany’s powerless plane plunged into the water and disappeared beneath the surface with rescuers unsure where he and his pilot had gone.
Dramatic dispatch audio captures crews calling for more ambulances, engines and boats as they raced to find the two men and tracked the last GPS location of a phone believed to be underwater.
"We’re going to be in search for a down plane," one responder warned.
WISCONSIN GOP GOVERNOR CANDIDATE SWIMS FROM SINKING PLANE AFTER EMERGENCY LAKE LANDING
First responders gather near a Lake Wausau boat landing during the rescue of Wisconsin gubernatorial candidate Tom Tiffany and his pilot. (WSAW)
Hours after leaving the hospital, Tiffany revealed Sunday that pilot Leonard "Len" Boltz had just seconds to react after the plane lost power on its final approach to Wausau Downtown Airport.
"Len said to me, ‘We are going down. Pull your seatbelt tight,’" Tiffany recalled during a news conference. "And that’s exactly what I did. I gave it a yank and pulled it good and tight."
COAST GUARD PLANE WITH DHS SECRETARY MARKWAYNE MULLIN ON BOARD MAKES EMERGENCY LANDING AFTER ENGINE FAILURE
Emergency crews search Lake Wausau after a plane carrying Wisconsin GOP gubernatorial candidate Tom Tiffany lost power and landed in the water. (WSAW)
"It was probably about 10 seconds later," he added. "We hit the water."
The impact sent Tiffany’s head into the dashboard, leaving him with a gash above his right eye that required 12 stitches. Boltz received four stitches for one of his injuries, Tiffany said.
PILOT'S BRAVERY ON DISPLAY IN STEERING CRIPPLED PLANE CLEAR OF TRAGEDY IN DRAMATIC WATER LANDING
The two men checked on each other before escaping through the passenger-side door as the plane began filling with water.
Tiffany searched the cockpit for his phone but could not find it. Boltz still had his phone and called 911.
PILOT DECLARES MAYDAY BEFORE SEAPLANE COMES DOWN IN NEW YORK CITY’S EAST RIVER
They climbed atop the slowly sinking plane and waited there for roughly 10 minutes as emergency lights appeared around the lake.

As the aircraft slipped underwater beneath them, they began swimming toward the airport. They made it roughly 100 to 150 feet before Tiffany reached a high spot in the lake where the water was about five feet deep.
MULTIPLE INJURED AFTER FLOATPLANE MAKES EMERGENCY LANDING, CATCHES FIRE OFF WASHINGTON COAST
FILE - Rep. Tom Tiffany was taken to the hospital after the small plane lost power and crashed into a lake. (Mark Schiefelbein-Pool/Getty Images)
"I said to Len, ‘Let’s just stay right here until help can come,’ because we could see the sirens," Tiffany said.
His voice cracked as the gravity of the ordeal appeared to catch up with him.
"We are just really fortunate," Tiffany said, pausing as he became emotional. "We’re really fortunate that God was looking after us last night."
The dispatch audio revealed the uncertainty confronting first responders as they raced toward different points along Lake Wausau.
"Can you get another ambulance rolling this way and one more engine, please?" one responder said. "Also page SAFER mutual aid to Bluegill Park with a boat."
Another responder reported that a witness had seen the aircraft go down but could provide only a general search area.
"I’m on scene with the reporting party," the responder said. "He stated he did see [an] aircraft crash."
4 FLORIDA FAMILY MEMBERS FOUND DEAD AFTER SMALL PLANE GOES DOWN OFF THE BAHAMAS
Crews carried thermal-imaging equipment and used a phone’s last known GPS coordinates to narrow the search. A landowner also provided a boat for deputies to use, according to the radio traffic.
"I was talking to the pilots," a responder said. "It sounds like they may plan to swim to the nearest shore after it went under, and then I lost contact with them."
"I believe his phone is underwater," he added. "They may be swimming south, I believe."
The tense search ended when rescuers announced that both men had been located.
"We have two victims in the water," a responder said. "We’re just pulling them out now."
Minutes later, a crew reported both were "alert, conscious" and confirmed everyone aboard the aircraft had been accounted for.
FILE - Republican U.S. Rep. Tom Tiffany, a candidate for Wisconsin governor, said he received stiches following the crash. (AP Photo/Scott Bauer)

Tiffany credited Boltz’s experience with keeping the emergency landing from becoming deadly. The former Air Force pilot trainer raised the plane’s landing gear before touching down, preventing it from potentially cartwheeling across the water.
"He was savvy enough and quick enough to think about, ‘We’ve got to make sure and pull that landing gear up,’" Tiffany said. "He did that, and it might have saved us."
Tiffany estimated the plane was still traveling between 70 and 80 mph when it hit the lake, describing the impact as "a fast-moving car crash."
"We’re fortunate the plane didn’t flip," he said. "I just take that to the skill of the pilot."
Wausau Mayor Doug Diny, a former military pilot, also praised Boltz for safely bringing the aircraft down at night.
PILOT RESCUED AFTER WORLD WAR II-ERA PLANE CRASHES AT PENNSYLVANIA AIRPORT
FILE - Republican Rep. Tom Tiffany of Wisconsin, a GOP gubernatorial candidate, said he plans to return to the campaign trail Monday. (Paul Steinhauser/Fox News)
"The last thing anyone wants to do as a pilot is put the aircraft in the water at night," Diny said.

Tiffany and Boltz were taken to Aspirus Wausau Hospital and released after treatment. Tiffany said a CT scan found no apparent concussion, though doctors instructed him to watch for possible symptoms and avoid flying for several days.
Despite canceling a trip to Washington, D.C., Tiffany said he plans to return to the campaign trail Monday.
"This will not deter me in my efforts that I started a year ago to become the next governor of the state of Wisconsin," he said.
The single-engine Beechcraft Bonanza remained submerged Sunday. The Federal Aviation Administration is investigating what caused it to lose power.
House Speaker Mike Johnson celebrated Tiffany’s return following the close call.
"Grateful to God no one was hurt in this accident and my good friend @TomTiffanyWI is safe and back on the trail!" Johnson wrote on X.
Tiffany represents Wisconsin’s 7th Congressional District and is running against Democratic Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley in November.

Crowley said he was grateful Tiffany and the pilot survived and praised Boltz’s actions.

title: Trump says Lindsay Clancy case is a ‘state situation' following attorney's pardon plea
summary: President Donald Trump expressed sympathy for the family of Lindsay Clancy’s three children while signaling that he would not intervene in the former nurse’s state murder case.
story: Retired Massachusetts Superior Court Judge Jack Lu told Fox News Digital a plea deal would be a "good idea" and in the public's "interest," but predicted prosecutors will again seek a first-degree murder conviction.

President Donald Trump on Sunday signaled that he would not intervene in the case of Massachusetts mother Lindsay Clancy, who is charged with killing her three young children amid allegations that she suffered from postpartum psychosis.
When asked whether he would pardon Clancy, Trump called the situation "very sad" but said the case is ultimately a "state situation," not a federal one.
"There’s no winner there. There’s no win no matter what you do. Three children are dead," he said.
LINDSAY CLANCY'S LAWYER REVEALS POST-MISTRIAL STRATEGY AS RETRIAL LOOMS
FILE — Trump expressed sympathy for the children’s deaths but said Clancy’s defense and the prosecution must resolve the case at the state level. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

The response came after Kevin Reddington, who represents Clancy, publicly asked Trump to grant his client a pardon last week. Reddington had acknowledged that Trump had no authority to issue a pardon in a state matter, but hoped he could still influence the outcome, according to his interview with WBZ-TV.
Trump indicated that the defense and prosecution need to resolve the legal matter at the local level while praising Reddington's work.
"He’s a good attorney. I’ve heard from other people he’s a very good attorney," Trump said. "I hope they can work it out. That’s something they have to work out … There is no win there."
LINDSAY CLANCY JUROR ADMITTED 'REASONABLE DOUBT' BUT STILL REFUSED INSANITY VERDICT, FOREPERSON SAYS
Lindsay Clancy arrives at court after being charged with three counts of first-degree murder in the deaths of her three children. (Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger via AP, Pool)
Previously, Trump said Clancy would still have to "pay the price" for the deaths of her three children.

"I assume there's going to be another trial. It's a terrible situation. Look, she did a horrible, horrible thing. Can't be worse. But you'll find out what the price to pay is. There'll be a price. It's going to be [a] mental institution or jail or something," he said.
Clancy, a 36-year-old former nurse, faces three counts of first-degree murder in the 2023 deaths of her children: 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 8-month-old Callan.
After their deaths, Clancy attempted to kill herself and was left paralyzed from the injuries.
Her defense attorneys have argued that Clancy suffered from postpartum psychosis, a severe but rare psychiatric condition that causes a sudden loss of reality after childbirth.

According to ABC, Reddington said Clancy had sought treatment from a psychiatrist he described as inexperienced. The psychiatrist reportedly prescribed her medications for postpartum depression in the months leading up to her reported psychotic break.
Callan, left, Dawson and Cora Clancy are pictured in an undated photo. The three children were killed at their home in Duxbury, Massachusetts, in January 2023. (Lindsay Marie Clancy/Facebook)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Clancy now faces a potential retrial after jurors deadlocked following a full week of deliberations, prompting Judge William Sullivan to declare a mistrial earlier this month.
The jury was split 11 to 1, with 11 jurors reportedly favoring an acquittal on the grounds that Clancy was not criminally responsible for the killings. The jury consisted of nine women and three men.
Fox News Digital’s Michael Ruiz and Elaine Mallon contributed to this report.
Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Trump tells Zelenskyy to stop doing 'one thing' during attacks on Russia
summary: President Donald Trump told reporters he wants Volodymyr Zelensky to stop hitting Russian diesel refineries, saying the strikes are causing a global fuel shortage.
story: President Donald Trump has a blunt message for Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as Kyiv continues targeting Russia: Stop hitting its diesel refineries.
President Donald Trump has a blunt message for Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as Kyiv continues targeting Russia: Stop hitting its diesel refineries.

Trump made the remarks Sunday while attending the Irish Open at his golf club in Doonbeg, Ireland, after a reporter asked whether he had spoken with Zelenskyy following a recent conversation with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
"Zelensky has to do one thing. He has to stop knocking out diesel fuel in Russia," Trump told reporters.
TRUMP NEGOTIATORS WITKOFF, KUSHNER MEET WITH PUTIN IN MOSCOW AS US PUSHES FOR END TO RUSSIA-UKRAINE WAR
FILE - President Donald Trump said he spoke with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky about the issue, noting there are other targets the country could focus on. (Getty Images)
Trump said Ukraine could continue pursuing other targets inside Russia but urged Zelenskyy to steer clear of the country’s diesel infrastructure.
"Let him go after targets, but not diesel fuel because he's causing a shortage of diesel," Trump said. "This isn't done by the Middle East. This is done by what's happening with Russia and Ukraine."
The president said he had already spoken directly with Zelenskyy about the issue.

"So we spoke to Mr. Zelensky about it. There are plenty of other targets," Trump said. "Don't hit diesel fuel because that's hurting the world. We don't want him to hit diesel fuel. He's hitting diesel refineries."
FILE - Trump said the military strikes are exacerbating a global diesel shortage. (Joe Raedle/Getty Images)
WATCH: FIGHTS BREAK OUT AT RUSSIAN GAS STATIONS AS PUTIN ADMITS FUEL SHORTAGES

Trump’s remarks come as Ukraine has targeted Russia’s oil and gas infrastructure with long-range strikes, part of Kyiv’s effort to hamper an industry that provides revenue and fuel for Moscow’s war effort. Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine more than four years ago.

The strikes have put pressure on Russia’s fuel supplies, prompting rationing in parts of the country and a Russian ban on diesel exports in July. The disruption has also added pressure to global diesel supplies, which have faced additional strain amid reduced oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.
Diesel prices in the U.S. climbed above an average of $6 per gallon on Friday, reaching a record high.
FILE - Diesel prices reached a record high in the U.S. on Friday. (Rebecca Noble/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
Russia has intensified its aerial attacks on Ukraine in recent weeks, including strikes involving ballistic missiles and drones, while Ukraine has continued targeting sites inside Russia.

Russian and Ukrainian officials reported another round of large-scale drone attacks overnight into Sunday, with casualties reported on both sides.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Election chaos in this red state just got even stranger for Republicans after Supreme Court ruling
summary: The Supreme Court blocked Missouri's new congressional map, forcing the state to use 2022 boundaries that favor Emanuel Cleaver's Kansas City district.
story: A major midterm shakeup unfolds as the Missouri Supreme Court blocks the state's new congressional map despite its use in primaries where over 1.2 million citizens voted. Missouri Gov. Mike Kehoe joins 'Fox & Friends' to discuss the ruling, which President Trump called a 'dark day.'
Republicans suffered a fresh blow in Missouri after the Supreme Court blocked a congressional map that could have helped the GOP gain another House seat in November.
The ruling, handed down last week, means Missouri will use its 2022 congressional map instead of the new boundaries backed by President Donald Trump and Missouri Republicans.

Missouri held its August primary under the new map, meaning candidates won their party nominations based on one set of district boundaries. But those boundaries will change before the November election, when Missouri is expected to return to its 2022 map.
TRUMP DANGLES $5,000 CHECKS AS DEBT SURGES — BUT ONLY IF GOP CAN CLEAR MAJOR MIDTERM HURDLE
People opposed to a congressional redistricting plan rally outside the Missouri Capitol in Jefferson City, Mo., Wednesday, Sept. 2, 2026. (AP Photo/David A. Lieb)

Typically, states redraw their congressional and state legislative districts once every decade after the Census to account for population changes and ensure that each district has roughly the same number of residents.
The new map would have shifted parts of Democratic Rep. Emanuel Cleaver’s Kansas City district into more Republican-leaning areas, making the seat more competitive.

Republicans hoped the changes would help them win seven of Missouri’s eight House seats in the November midterm elections. The GOP currently holds six of the state’s eight seats, while Democrats hold two.
Missouri must now use the 2022 map, which keeps Cleaver’s district more favorable to Democrats.

The maps show how Missouri’s congressional districts changed between 2022 and 2025, including the expansion of the Kansas City-area 5th District into more Republican-leaning rural parts of the state. (Missouri Office of Administration/Amanda Macias/Fox News Digital)
The Supreme Court’s decision came after more than a year of legal battles over which congressional map Missouri should use.

Missouri held its August primary under the new map, but the state will use its 2022 district boundaries for the November general election. That means some voters could be assigned to a different congressional district in November than the one in which they voted during the primary.
The change could affect more than 1 million voters, or nearly one-fourth of Missouri’s electorate, according to an Associated Press estimate.
The conflicting court orders have added to the confusion, with the November election just weeks away. Candidates and election officials must now adjust to the 2022 boundaries.
MISSOURI HIGH COURT BLOCKS GOP-BACKED CONGRESSIONAL MAPS AHEAD OF MIDTERMS; TRUMP BLASTS 'RIDICULOUS' RULING
The Supreme Court blocked Missouri from using a GOP-backed congressional map that could have helped Republicans gain a House seat in November. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)
The Supreme Court did not explain its reasoning in the brief order.

The White House did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.
Amanda Macias covers the intersection of business, economics and politics, with a focus on how policy decisions shape markets, businesses and American workers.

title: Trump gives Smithsonian days to replace 'strange modernist sculpture' with Founding Father
summary: President Donald Trump demands a 30-foot George Washington statue replace the "Infinity" sculpture outside the National Museum of American History in Washington.
story: 'The Ingraham Angle' host Laura Ingraham exposes how progressive curators inside the Smithsonian are rewriting American history through radical exhibitions. Historian Dr. Jody Edward Ginn analyzes the systemic exclusion of conservative perspectives, noting that a new exhibit features three times more liberal items than conservative ones. Ginn discusses how the progressive shift raises concerns about the political neutralization of America's national museums.
President Donald Trump is calling on the Smithsonian to replace a decades-old modernist sculpture outside the National Museum of American History with a towering, 30-foot statue of George Washington.

In social media posts late Friday, Trump said the "Infinity" sculpture that has stood outside the museum since 1967 "says nothing about America," while Washington, he argued, "more than anyone else, says everything about America."
Trump also called for the museum to open a five-year exhibition honoring Washington that would run through Feb. 22, 2032, the 300th anniversary of the first president’s birth.
INSIDE THE BEHEMOTH SMITHSONIAN MUSEUM NETWORK DRAWING FIRE FROM THE TRUMP ADMINISTRATION

People walking past the "Infinity" sculpture outside the Smithsonian National Museum of American History on the National Mall in Washington, Tuesday, Sept. 8, 2026. (AP Photo/Pablo Martinez Monsivais)

Trump also wants the Smithsonian to install an 11-foot statue of Washington in the museum’s Flag Hall by Constitution Day on Sept. 17. The statue was featured at the recent Freedom 250 Grand Prix race.
"Immediately design and display a five-year exhibition worthy of the Life, Sacrifice, and Contributions of George Washington," Trump wrote.
"Then, as soon as it is ready, install a 30-foot Washington Colossus where ‘Infinity’ stands today," he added.
"Infinity," created by New York artist José de Rivera, was commissioned by the federal government and installed outside the museum in 1967.

President Donald Trump has argued the Smithsonian should place greater emphasis on America's founding principles, national achievements and patriotic history. (Maxine Wallace/The Washington Post/Getty Images)

It is unclear whether Trump can order the Smithsonian to make the changes. The institution is outside the executive branch and is overseen by a Board of Regents that includes Vice President JD Vance, Chief Justice John Roberts, lawmakers from both parties and citizen members.
Fox News Digital reached out to the Smithsonian for comment but did not immediately receive a response.
Trump has repeatedly criticized how the Smithsonian presents American history, particularly as the country celebrates its 250th anniversary.
EXCAVATION SET TO BEGIN ON TRUMP ADMINISTRATION'S 250-FOOT TRIUMPHAL ARCH AMID LEGAL BATTLE
In his posts Friday, he accused the National Museum of American History of giving too little attention to Washington and other Founding Fathers.
Trump singled out Washington’s crossing of the Delaware River on Christmas night in 1776 and the American victory at Trenton, saying the museum does not give those events the attention they deserve.

This painting, Washington Crossing the Delaware (by Emanuel Leutze, American, 1816 - 1868), 1851, shows George Washington's crossing of the Delaware River on the night of December 25-26, 1776, as part of a surprise sneak attack on the British Army during the American Revolutionary War. (GraphicaArtis via Getty Images)
"He is easily America’s Greatest Hero," Trump wrote of Washington. "Without him, our Country and our Freedoms wouldn’t exist."
Trump also criticized the Smithsonian’s recently ended Center for Restorative History, an initiative created to spotlight stories that have been excluded from the national historical narrative.
Trump said the museum should instead create a "Center for American Heroes."

"Tell the stories of Americans who faced great challenges, overcame them, built great things, defended our Country, made America better, and helped our Nation more fully live up to our Founding Ideals," he wrote.
SUPREME COURT CHIEF JUSTICE PRAISES OUTGOING SMITHSONIAN LEADER WHO WAS UNDER PRESSURE FROM TRUMP ADMIN
Those criticisms have also led to action by the White House.
In March 2025, Trump signed an executive order aimed at eliminating what the White House called "divisive narratives" and "improper ideology" at the Smithsonian.
The White House followed this year with a report criticizing the Smithsonian, including what it said was a lack of attention to Washington and other Founding Fathers.
The Smithsonian National Museum of American History in Washington, D.C., on Sunday, Oct. 12, 2025. (Stefani Reynolds/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
In July, Trump ordered his administration to place signs outside the National Museum of American History telling visitors that some exhibits are inaccurate.
In a statement last year, the Smithsonian’s Board of Regents said it was committed to keeping the institution nonpartisan and its scholarship free from political or partisan influence.
The board also acknowledged that the Smithsonian "can and must do more" and directed its leadership to ensure museum content is unbiased.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Smithsonian secretary Lonnie Bunch announced last week that he will step down at the end of the year.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: GOP women sound alarm as Lindsay Clancy backlash revives calls to repeal 19th Amendment: ‘Definitely a threat’
summary: Republican women warn that online calls to repeal the 19th Amendment after the Lindsay Clancy trial could alienate female voters from the GOP.
story: Republican women Mehek Cooke and Tiffany Losee react to how online calls to repeal the 19th Amendment impact the GOP after Lindsay Clancy's high-profile case sparked online debate over women's voting rights.
If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 1-800-273-TALK (8255).
Calls to repeal women’s rights to vote are emerging from the online firestorm over the Lindsay Clancy trial, prompting Republican women to warn that the intraparty rhetoric could hurt the GOP.
"I think there’s definitely a threat in the Republican Party right now," political and legal strategist Mehek Cooke told Fox News Digital.

The online calls to repeal the 19th Amendment come after Clancy’s high-profile murder trial ended in a mistrial, with 11 of the 12 jurors favoring a verdict of not guilty by reason of insanity. Clancy admitted to killing her three children, but her defense argued she was not criminally responsible because she was suffering from postpartum psychosis.
LINDSAY CLANCY MISTRIAL DECLARED AFTER JURY DEADLOCKS IN KILLINGS OF HER THREE CHILDREN
Lindsay Clancy listens to testimony Aug. 10, 2026. (Greg Derr/Pool/The Patriot Ledger)
"Convict Clancy. Also Repeal the 19th Amendment!" one user posted on X.

"The female jurors in the Lindsay Clancy trial are speaking out about their deliberations and disagreements with the sole male holdout. The more they speak the better they make the case for repealing the 19th Amendment," another user posted.
Cooke warned that calls to strip women of the right to vote, largely coming from accounts identifying as conservative, risk alienating female voters from the Republican Party.
"When you have these fringe activists online talking about repealing the 19th Amendment or alienating women, it really doesn’t help," Cooke said.

The calls followed after the case made waves on social media, particularly after hundreds of mostly female Clancy supporters gathered outside a Massachusetts courthouse during the murder trial. The demonstrators rallying behind Clancy argued the case is an example of the lack of understanding of postpartum depression.
ROGAN SHREDS SUPPORTERS OF LINDSAY CLANCY, SAYS THEY WOULDN'T RALLY IF A FATHER WERE ON TRIAL FOR SAME CRIME
Supporters of Lindsay Clancy gather outside of Plymouth Superior Court Aug. 20, 2026. (John Tlumacki/The Boston Globe via Getty Images)
But the demonstrations quickly turned into ammunition for online critics who argued that the support for Clancy is an indication that women should be stripped of their right to vote.

"This Lindsay Clancy trial has shown us How spiteful women can be, the fact that women are willing to even defend a child killer just because they want to be ok with the "sisterhood" should alarm you," another user wrote on X.
"They will gaslight you, they will use sign language against you and even try to call you all sort of names. But guess what, they are still wrong and they know it. Repeal the 19th."
Cooke pushed back on the idea that the calls to repeal the 19th Amendment reflect the reality of the mainstream Republican Party.
"Social media isn’t real life," Cooke said. "I think a lot of people out there put these arbitrary crazy ideas, but it doesn’t really reflect what normal people think and what mainstream thinks.
LINDSAY CLANCY MURDER TRIAL BECOMES SOCIAL MEDIA OBSESSION AS TIKTOKERS, SLEUTHS DEBATE CONTROVERSIAL CASE
A protester holds a "Repeal the 19th" sign amid an online debate over women’s voting rights following the Lindsay Clancy trial. (Joseph Prezioso/AFP via Getty Images)

"I think you're getting these calls because of where our culture is today. You looked at the Lindsay Clancy trial and all the women out there in pink that were continuing to support a woman who murdered three children. You're constantly seeing this cultural push in terms of where women stand today in politics."
Tiffany Losee, director of fundraising for The Conservative Caucus, told Fox News Digital that Democrats are to blame for pushing out this agenda and associating it with the broader Republican Party.
"You have to understand this is all a game to the Democrat Party," Losee said. "They’re going to push out anything that looks fringe on the right."

Losee also claimed that Democrats are using this rhetoric on the right to distract voters from the rise of socialism that has emerged within the Democratic Party, claiming if voters understood the ideals of the party, they would "run faster than imaginable to get away from such government control."
HOW THE 'LONG MARCH' THROUGH THE INSTITUTIONS LED TO SOCIALIST TAKEOVER OF DEM PARTY: 'NEED TO WAKE UP'

"They're gonna push out crazy Lindsay Clancy ideas or ‘look over here at something shiny, or communism is cool, socialism is cool, everything's free,'" Losee said. "But then they will not take that extra step to educate the voter on what exactly they are pushing."

Cooke and Losee spoke to Fox News Digital on the issue as Republicans gathered in Dallas for the party’s first-ever midterm convention, where the GOP gathered to rally its base to vote as Republicans work to stay in control of Congress as November’s midterm elections approach.

"I think the left has constantly alienated women," Cooke said. "It's our responsibility to pull them in and show them common sense."
Hannah is a Production Assistant for the Politics team at Fox News Digital.

title: Vulnerable House Republicans embrace Trump as GOP bets on defying midterm history
summary: President Donald Trump urged Republicans to "pretend that I'm on the ballot," as vulnerable GOP incumbents rallied at the first-ever midterm convention.
story: Reps. Ryan Mackenzie and Mike Lawler, along with candidate Eric Flores, told Fox News Digital why they're aligning with President Donald Trump ahead of November's GOP midterm elections.
DALLAS — President Donald Trump is getting a much warmer reception from his fellow Republicans during this election cycle than his predecessor did from Democrats this time two years ago.

Conventional political wisdom dictates that the party in power will suffer losses in Congress during a midterm election year. Americans who oppose the president's party are typically more motivated to vote than people who support their agenda.

But the GOP is banking on the opposite effect. The first-ever GOP midterm convention featured back-to-back keynote addresses from the commander in chief, as well as speeches from his Cabinet officials, allies and members of Congress.

"I'm asking you to pretend that I'm on the ballot," Trump told his audience on Wednesday. Republican incumbents and candidates running in battleground districts this November also took the stage, and all speakers projected confidence despite Trump's own low approval numbers.
DEMOCRATS TARGETING 12 ADDITIONAL RED DISTRICTS IN MIDTERMS PUSH TO RETAKE HOUSE
President Donald Trump speaks during the Republican convention at American Airlines Center Sept. 9, 2026, in Dallas. (The Dallas Morning News via Getty Images)

"We ran together in 2024 on a ticket with President Trump, [Sen. Dave McCormick, R-Pa.] and myself. Voters elected all of us to deliver real change and results, and we've actually been able to do that with securing the border and delivering historic tax relief," Rep. Ryan Mackenzie, R-Pa., told Fox News Digital on the sidelines of the convention.
"Now what we're seeing is, in a midterm, we are actually going to defy the historic trends. Why is that? Because the Democrats are so far left they are totally out of touch."

Republicans believe their warnings of Democrats' socialist insurgency will help them keep their majorities in the House and Senate this year, along with touting Trump's signature tax cuts in the One Big, Beautiful Bill Act.
HOW ONE NYC SUBURB COULD DECIDE WHICH PARTY CONTROLS THE HOUSE
Mackenzie is one of Democrats' top targets in the election cycle, along with Rep. Mike Lawler, R-N.Y., in the suburbs outside New York City.

"He's the president of the United States, and whether it was Joe Biden or Donald Trump, I've always shown up," Lawler told Fox News Digital. "You have to be able to engage with the president, and, you know, frankly, this is where I think the Democrats have made a very big mistake. They could get a lot more in terms of what it is that they want if they would actually engage constructively."
Lawler, Mackenzie and Rep. Rob Bresnahan, R-Pa., are the three vulnerable incumbents who took the stage during the convention last week.

Rep. Mike Lawler, R-N.Y., speaks with local law enforcement about the rise of antisemitism in New York City during a campaign endorsement event at Haverstraw Elks Lodge No. 877 in Haverstraw, N.Y. (Kyle Mazza/CNP)
TRUMP HITS KEY BATTLEGROUNDS TO SELL TAX CUTS, BOOST GOP AHEAD OF MIDTERMS

Lawler, for his part, introduced two residents from his district whose daughter was killed by an illegal immigrant in Chicago, a poignant symbol of what Republicans say could happen more often if Democrats win.
Trump has also campaigned in each of their districts in recent months as he crisscrosses the country in a bid to keep control of Congress for the latter half of his final term.
But it was not just vulnerable incumbents who appeared in Dallas alongside Trump. The two-day affair also brought candidates from across the country, even those running in tight races.
GOP FACES BRUTAL MIDTERM HEADWINDS AS REPUBLICANS PAINT ELECTION AS ‘COMPETITION WITH COMMUNISM’

"When people say that folks are running away from President Trump, I'll tell you, I'm certainly not doing that. And let me tell you why: Because he has made promises to South Texas, and he has kept them, especially when we look at border security," candidate Eric Flores told Fox News Digital.
JOHNSON DOWNPLAYS GOP'S MIDTERM WOES AS DEMOCRATS EYE HOUSE TAKEOVER: 'I AM VERY BULLISH'

"My opponent, who said, you know, that the sleepy Joe Biden administration and the no-show border czar, Kamala Harris, were on the right track. Let me tell you firsthand, I was on Operation Guardian support, was a federal prosecutor on the border. It was a humanitarian crisis. President Trump, on day one, secured our border."
Flores is running in a South Texas district represented by Rep. Vicente Gonzalez, D-Texas.
Time will tell if the strategy pays off, but Democrats are already seizing on it in hopes that associating with Trump will sink GOP candidates like it did in 2018.
TRUMP'S APPROVAL RATING PLUMMETS TO NEW LOW AHEAD OF CRITICAL MIDTERMS: 'MORE WORK TO DO'
Rep. Ryan Mackenzie, R-Pa., during an event on inflation at Mount Airy Casino Resort in Mount Pocono, Pa., Dec. 9, 2025. (Adam Gray/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

"Ryan Mackenzie, Rob Bresnahan and Scott Perry made their priorities clear tonight: They care more about Donald Trump’s cost-raising agenda than what’s best for the people of Pennsylvania," Pennsylvania Democratic Party Chair Eugene DePasquale said in a statement.

"After jetting all the way to Texas to champion an agenda of higher gas prices, cost-raising tariffs and healthcare cuts, Mackenzie, Bresnahan, Perry and the entire PA GOP have proven that they’ll put Trump ahead of our Commonwealth every single time, and Pennsylvanians are ready to send them packing this November."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Fox News Digital did not see Rep. Scott Perry, R-Pa., who is also expected to run a close race, at the convention, but reached out to his campaign for comment.
Elizabeth Elkind is a politics reporter for Fox News Digital leading coverage of the House of Representatives. Previous digital bylines seen at Daily Mail and CBS News.

title: GOP rising star reveals how Republicans can lock down minority voters without Trump on ballot
summary: T.W. Shannon says Donald Trump transformed the GOP into a working party, pointing to job creation and lower crime as keys to winning Black voters.
story: Trump cracked Democrats’ grip on Black voters, and GOP leader T.W. Shannon of Oklahoma tells Fox News Digital there’s no going back.

DALLAS — While President Donald Trump will not be on the ballot for the 2026 midterm elections, the former chair of Black Voices for Trump believes Republicans can maintain the momentum gained from his major performance improvements among Black voters during the 2024 presidential race.

T.W. Shannon, a former Oklahoma state House Speaker who served last year in the second Trump administration and is now the Republican lieutenant governor nominee in his home state, says policies "the GOP has expressed," as well as the Democratic Party's leftward lurch, will help Republicans as they continue to court Black voters.
Trump won 16% of the Black vote in the 2024 presidential election, according to a Fox News Voter Analysis, nearly double his total four years earlier.
DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB
President Donald Trump arrives to speak during the first day of the Republican Midterm Convention at the American Airlines Center in Dallas, Texas, Wednesday, Sept. 9, 2026. (Bloomberg)

"It's because Donald Trump has transformed the Republican Party back into the working party. You see Democrats competing for the Black vote now. Something that you used to not see at all. They didn't have to, they just took it for granted," Shannon said in a Fox News Digital interview Thursday on the sidelines of the first-ever GOP midterm convention.
Shannon pointed to job creation and declining crime rates during the second Trump administration and said, "These are things that actually benefit ... Black voters and Black communities."
He then took aim at Democratic candidates backed by or aligned with the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA).
SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

"Look at what … the DSA is offering, you know. We're talking about raising taxes. We're talking about doing away with the Senate ... disbanding the police," he said. "These are not things that are well received in the Black community."
Democrats disagree with Shannon's assessment.

"Black Americans are going to reject Trump’s billionaires-first, cost-raising agenda at the ballot box this November and elect Democrats who are fighting to lower costs and deliver for working families," a Democratic National Committee (DNC) spokesperson told Fox News Digital.

The spokesperson added that the "DNC is investing critical resources to reach, register and mobilize Black voters across the country. While the Trump administration continues to attack civil and voting rights, we are fighting to protect the core of our democracy."

Shannon, a Lawton native who became his state's youngest and first African American House speaker in 2013 and the first member of the Chickasaw Nation to hold the office, is favored to win in November in solidly Republican Oklahoma.

He said speaking in primetime at the convention gave him a chance to stand on the "national stage."
"Any time I get a chance to tell the story about how great Oklahoma is and how great America is, I won't miss a chance to do it," he said.
Paul Steinhauser covers the national campaign trail from coast to coast for Fox News

title: Wisconsin GOP governor candidate swims from sinking plane after emergency lake landing
summary: Wisconsin Republican Tom Tiffany says he and the pilot swam from a sinking Bonanza after an emergency water landing in Lake Wausau Saturday night.
story: Police responded Sunday to a Wisconsin lake where a plane carrying gubernatorial candidate Rep. Tom Tiffany crash-landed, forcing Tiffany and the pilot to swim to safety as the aircraft sank. (WSAW)

Wisconsin Republican gubernatorial candidate and U.S. Rep. Tom Tiffany said he and a pilot escaped with minor injuries after their small plane lost power and made an emergency landing in a lake Saturday night.
Tiffany said the four-seat Bonanza was approaching Wausau Downtown Airport when it lost power after his appearance at the La Crosse County Lincoln Day Dinner.
"The pilot made an emergency water landing in Lake Wausau," Tiffany wrote on X.
COAST GUARD PLANE WITH DHS SECRETARY MARKWAYNE MULLIN ON BOARD MAKES EMERGENCY LANDING AFTER ENGINE FAILURE
Republican U.S. Rep. Tom Tiffany, a candidate for Wisconsin governor, gives a news conference Jan. 26, 2026, in Madison, Wis. (AP Photo/Scott Bauer)
The congressman explained that he and the pilot quickly called 911 after hitting the water, but the aircraft began filling and sinking into the lake before rescuers could reach them.
Tiffany's campaign later released a statement explaining the circumstances of the crash and the candidate's injuries.

"Tom suffered a laceration above his right eye that required stitches and was released from the hospital last night. The pilot was also released. Tom and his family thank God that neither suffered more serious injuries and are grateful for the exceptional care he received at Aspirus Wausau Hospital," the statement said.
"As the plane began to submerge, we exited the aircraft and swam to a shallow area, where we waited until emergency responders reached us by boat," Tiffany said.
MULTIPLE INJURED AFTER FLOATPLANE MAKES EMERGENCY LANDING, CATCHES FIRE OFF WASHINGTON COAST
Republican Rep. Tom Tiffany of Wisconsin, a GOP gubernatorial candidate, speaks at a campaign event in Oconomowoc, Wis., Aug. 10, 2026. (Paul Steinhauser/Fox News)
Tiffany and the pilot were pulled from the lake and transported to Aspirus Wausau Hospital. Both sustained only minor injuries, according to the congressman.

Tiffany and the pilot were the only two people on board the Beechcraft K35. The investigation into the loss of power will be handled by the Federal Aviation Administration and the National Transportation Safety Board, the campaign says.
Tiffany shared that his wife, Chris, was by his side at the hospital after the harrowing landing and water rescue.

summary: A woman twice showed up uninvited at Kamala Harris and Doug Emhoff's $8 million Malibu home, prompting security to call the sheriff late Friday evening.
story: Former Vice President Kamala Harris speaks at a Democratic fireside chat, labeling the Trump administration 'the most corrupt, callous and incompetent presidential administration we've ever seen.' After the woman was dropped off by an Uber, she attempted to contact security at the $8 million home and was told she needed to leave, according to the California Post.

SUSPECT ARRESTED AT KIM KARDASHIAN'S MANSION AFTER STOLEN VEHICLE, BREAK-IN REPORTED IN HIDDEN HILLS

title: Dem handlers lash out when cameraman confronts their boss about debate: ‘No pictures’
summary: Video shows Amy Acton's campaign staff confronting a cameraman who asked why she refuses to debate Vivek Ramaswamy in the Ohio governor race.
story: Amy Acton's campaign staff shield her from a videographer in video obtained by Fox News Digital. (Obtained by Fox News Digital)

Campaign personnel for Amy Acton, Ohio’s former health director and Democratic candidate for Ohio governor, got into a confrontation with a Republican political activist wielding a camera last Saturday at one of Acton’s campaign events in Harrison, Ohio.
When the cameraman approached Acton, asking her why she continued to decline invitations to debate her Republican challenger, Vivek Ramaswamy, her staff quickly rushed in to block him off from Acton.

The video, which shows Acton walking away from the interviewer, adds to criticisms from Ramaswamy’s camp that she hasn’t given a good answer for why she isn’t willing to do a debate as both candidates enter the homestretch of their campaigns.
RAMASWAMY PUMPS $25M OF OWN CASH INTO OHIO GOVERNOR BID, SMASHES FUNDRAISING RECORDS WITH $50 MILLION HAUL

Democratic gubernatorial candidate Dr. Amy Acton speaks at a primary election night campaign event after winning the party's nomination for governor in Columbus, Ohio, Tuesday, May 5, 2026. (Jay LaPrete/AP Photo)
"Dr. Amy Acton, why do you refuse to debate your opponent, Vivek Ramaswamy?" the interviewer asked.
"No photos, no videos," the staff repeated. "I said — no pictures, no interviews."
At one point in the confrontation, Acton’s staff seemed to have bumped into the cameraman, jolting his camera out of frame and prompting him to ask them to be "careful."
Acton did not respond to the questions.
Earlier this month, after Ramaswamy accepted a debate invitation from CNN, Acton’s campaign told local media she would not accept.

"Dr. Acton’s focus is on talking with Ohioans, not platforming a scam artist who spreads baseless lies about her and her family, uses AI to falsely paint her as someone with a substance abuse problem, and shames Dr. Acton for being sexually abused as a child while Vivek stands with predators and abusers," a campaign spokesperson said in a Sept. 2 statement.
ARMED MAN ACCUSED OF LUNGING AT OHIO DEM CANDIDATE AVOIDS FELONIES AS PROSECUTOR REVEALS KEY EVIDENCE
Ohio Republican guebenatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy speaks during a campaign rally on Feb. 25, 2025 at the Glass City Center in Toledo, Ohio. (Scott W. Grau/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)
TOP ELECTION SCHEMES ROILING KEY MIDTERM RACES AS BOTH PARTIES ACCUSE RIVALS OF TRICKERY

The response refers to a series of Republican attacks: her role in Ohio’s COVID response, a verbal domestic dispute in 2019 that she had while intoxicated, and AI-generated campaign ads that replaced her car’s license plate with a "drunk mom" tag. It also nods to Ramaswamy’s quiet posture toward releasing the Epstein files at the outset of his gubernatorial campaign.
In his response, Ramaswamy ignored Acton’s needling.
He seized on her decision, calling into question her qualifications to lead the state as its top executive while, at the same time, refusing to press her case on a debate stage.

"It’s too bad for Ohio voters that Acton won’t take voter questions, won’t debate, quit after failing as Ohio’s health director, and has some serious issues now surfaced in multiple police reports," Ramaswamy said in a post to social media.
FOX NEWS POLL: ECONOMIC ANXIETY AND CANDIDATE CONCERNS DEFINE OHIO SENATE RACE

Amy Acton, former director of the Ohio Department of Health and Democratic gubernatorial candidate, meets with local residents while campaigning at Bottoms Up Coffee in Columbus, Ohio, on Monday, April 6, 2026. (Stephen Zenner/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

title: Blue state governor's pardon of convicted felon torpedos a major Supreme Court immigration fight
summary: Kathy Hochul pardoned a convicted noncitizen, effectively mooting a Supreme Court case on bond hearing rights for detained immigrants facing deportation.
story: DHS general counsel James Percival warns of an 'epidemic of judicial activism' after a federal judge in California orders the release of an MS-13 murder suspect. Percival argues that individuals wanted for murder must remain in immigration detention during removal proceedings.

The Supreme Court will no longer hear an oral argument for a case centered on bond rights for noncitizens detained for lengthy periods, ruling the case moot after New York Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul pardoned a lawfully present Dominican citizen, who pleaded guilty to second-degree assault.

Hochul pardoned Keisy Guerrero Mariano, who is identified in court documents as "Keisy GM," in late August, effectively killing the Trump administration's appeal to the Supreme Court arguing that noncitizens, including those with green card status, do not have a legal right to a bond hearing for a prolonged detention if they have committed crimes that are grounds for mandatory deportation.
Hochul, who is staunchly opposed to President Donald Trump's immigration enforcement crackdown, issued the pardon for Mariano just as the brief was due.
FEDERAL APPEALS COURT COMPARES TRUMP MIGRANT DETENTION POLICY TO JAPANESE AMERICAN INTERNMENT
FILE - New York Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul pardoned Keisy Guerrero Mariano in late August. (Adam Gray/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Solicitor General John Sauer agreed Friday that Genalo v. Black is now moot, but said the Trump administration will seek an "alternative vehicle" to challenge the Second Circuit’s 2024 ruling that prolonged immigration detention can trigger a constitutional right to a bond hearing.
Sauer said the administration intends to find another case through which the Supreme Court can resolve the issue during its 2026-27 term.
The lawsuit centered on the challenges of plaintiffs Carol Williams Black, a Jamaican national with lawful standing, and Mariano — both convicted criminals detained by ICE.
APPEALS COURT BLOCKS TRUMP ADMIN FROM HOLDING MIGRANTS WITHOUT BOND FOR OVER 90 DAYS
Mariano was first arrested by Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers in 2020 over a 2015 second-degree assault conviction for which he served time, making him eligible for deportation.
He spent nearly two years in ICE detention, but was released in 2022 due to a nationwide injunction that required the release of detainees because of COVID-19 health risks.
Prior to his release, Judge John P. Cronan of the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York denied Mariano's habeas corpus request in November 2021.
FILE - Mariano was released in 2022 after spending nearly two years in ICE detention. (Getty Images)

But in May 2024, the Second Circuit overruled Cronan's decision, ruling that the government must grant noncitizens a bond hearing once detention becomes "unreasonably long." Failure to do so, the court ruled, would violate the Fifth Amendment's due process clause.

The case was appealed to the Supreme Court, which agreed to hear the case June 15; however, the high court ruled Black's case moot because he had left the United States and filed a court declaration that he would not be returning to the country.
Black was convicted in New York in 2000 of sexually abusing a minor under the age of 11.

FILE - Following an appeal, the Second Circuit ruled the government must grant noncitizens a bond hearing once detention becomes "unreasonably long." (Dominic Gwinn/Middle East Images/AFP via Getty Images)
DHS BLASTS MINNESOTA BOARD FOR UNANIMOUSLY PARDONING ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CONVICTED OF 3 ASSAULTS
Hochul's decision to issue a pardon to Mariano has garnered fierce criticism from legal experts.

"Pretty wild to fully pardon an aggravated felon to (1) stop the felon from getting deported and (2) stop the Supreme Court from ruling on an issue. (Especially as this litigation has been going on for years)," Eric Wessan, Iowa’s solicitor general, posted on X.
He praised Sauer's decision to fight back on the Second Circuit's ruling.
"I wonder how many non-American felons Governors like Hochul will choose to fully pardon and free to avoid them facing consequences for their actions," Wessan added.

title: The one line from JD Vance’s GOP keynote that reveals his vision for America
summary: JD Vance framed the midterm elections as a fight over every American child's birthright in a Dallas keynote that previewed his post-Trump GOP vision.
story: The vice president says the Democratic Party now boasts members who do not love America.

Vice President JD Vance used his keynote address at the Republican midterm convention Thursday to frame the November elections as a fight over America’s future, arguing that every child is entitled to inherit the country’s opportunities regardless of background.

The speech also gave Vance one of his most prominent national platforms since becoming vice president to define his own political vision, as he emerges as a central figure in the GOP’s post-Trump future and speculation continues about a potential 2028 presidential campaign.

"Every American child is born an heir, born with the right to inherit the blessings of the greatest country on Earth — not because of who their parents are, what they look like or where they come from, but because they are Americans and this is our country," Vance said in Dallas.
"And that birthright, ladies and gentlemen, is what this November is all about," he added.
VANCE, CRUZ, HEAD TO IOWA ON 2026 MISSIONS AS 2028 GOP RACE TO SUCCEED TRUMP HEATS UP
Vice President JD Vance used his keynote speech to rally Republicans ahead of the midterms while offering a glimpse of his vision for the GOP’s future. (Brandon Bell/Getty Images)

Vance tied that idea to his own family, speaking about the birth of his fourth child, Alec, six weeks ago. He said he wants his son and all American children to grow up with access to clean water, healthy food, a quality education, safe communities and the opportunity to afford a home and raise a family.
He also connected that vision to the legacy of his late friend Charlie Kirk, who was killed one year ago. Vance said Kirk encouraged young men to fall in love, start families and become fathers.

The speech marked a shift from the personal story of Vance’s Appalachian upbringing that he emphasized during the 2024 Republican convention. Instead, Vance presented himself as a father focused on the country his children will inherit, while using the platform to preview the issues and themes that could define his future in the Republican Party.
TRUMP DANGLES $5,000 CHECKS AS DEBT SURGES — BUT ONLY IF GOP CAN CLEAR MAJOR MIDTERM HURDLE
Vance used his speech to accuse Democrats of abandoning working-class Americans and becoming the "party of hatred," while urging Republicans to turn out in November. (Al Drago/Bloomberg/Getty Images)

Vance then pivoted from his family-focused message to a sweeping attack on the Democratic Party. He accused Democrats of abandoning working-class Americans and becoming increasingly hostile toward the country’s traditional values.
"The Democrats are the party of hatred," Vance said. "They’re the party that despises America and the people who built it."
FOLLOW FOX NEWS DIGITAL’S COVERAGE OF THE GOP’S 2026 MIDTERM CONVENTION

Vance’s keynote also underscored his growing profile as a potential 2028 Republican presidential contender, even as he has said he will wait until after the midterm elections before deciding whether to run. (Tasos Katopodis/Getty Images)
He urged Republicans to view the November election as more than a traditional partisan contest.

"This November is so much more than red team versus blue team," Vance said. "It’s about fighting for our fellow citizens, for their dreams, and for the inheritance of a great nation that all of us are going to leave behind."

The speech placed family, faith and national identity at the center of Vance’s midterm message while offering a glimpse of how he could define himself within the Republican Party beyond President Donald Trump.

title: Abdul El-Sayed touts ‘whole a--’ medical credentials while defending sex changes for children
summary: Abdul El-Sayed, a Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate candidate, argues 'whole a--' doctors should decide trans treatment without government interference.
story: The Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate candidate argued that medical decisions should be left to patients, parents and doctors, who went to "whole a--" medical school.

Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed said the government should not restrict sex changes, arguing that "whole a--" doctors like himself should be allowed to make their own determinations for patients' treatment plans.

The remarks came during El-Sayed's Friday rally held at Michigan State University, during which the former Detroit Health Department head responded to a student's question about protecting sex changes. Since launching his campaign, El-Sayed has flaunted that he is a "physician" and, if elected, he would be the first doctor to serve as a Democratic senator in 50 years. However, Fox News Digital previously reported El-Sayed has never held a medical license in Michigan or New York.

"I went to a whole a-- medical school, everybody I graduated with also went to whole a-- medical school," El-Sayed said. "And then... they went to whole a-- residency. Right? And some of them went to whole a-- fellowship. They took whole a-- exams to provide whole a-- healthcare."
DEM SENATE HOPEFUL’S ‘PHYSICIAN’ CAMPAIGN PITCH UNDER FIRE AFTER LICENSE RECORDS REVEAL KEY GAPS

Abdul El-Sayed answers a question during a press conference at the Michigan Democratic Party State Endorsement Convention in Detroit on April 19, 2026. El-Sayed has never held a medical license in Michigan or New York. (Jose Juarez/AP Photo)

"They are the experts that a patient wants to see when they seek care," El-Sayed continued. "And the decision about what healthcare is necessary ought to be held between a patient — and or their parents if they're under the age of 18 — and their doctor. That's it."
The remarks come as the Trump administration has made major strides in restricting minors' access to "sex-rejecting" procedures, which include hormone therapy and surgeries.

Earlier this week, the Justice Department announced that Mount Sinai had joined other hospitals, like Texas Children's Hospital, the Cleveland Clinic Foundation and Connecticut Children's Hospital, to halt sex change procedures for children after reaching an agreement with the Trump administration.
MEDICAID ENDS FUNDING FOR CHILD SEX-CHANGE PROCEDURES AS TRUMP ADMIN SLAMS 'EXPERIMENTAL' TREATMENTS

El-Sayed has made the promise of "Medicare-for-all" — government-run healthcare — as the major selling point of his campaign; he said that even though the government will be covering the bill, it needs to stay out of the doctor's decisions about a patient's treatment plan.

"I don't think the government gets to have a say about what healthcare is provided in what circumstances and why," El-Sayed said. "And to me, that is the standard on which we decide how we make healthcare decisions."
THE MEDICARE FOR ALL TRADE-OFFS SOCIALISTS AREN'T TALKING ABOUT, ACCORDING TO EXPERTS
A protester holds a sign in support of sex changes for transgender children outside the U.S. Supreme Court in Washington, D.C., on June 18, 2025. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

"Not what the government says you can or can't do, but what a patient and/or their parent, if they're under 18, and their provider to decide. That's the most important thing," El-Sayed continued. "And there's a lot of disinformation about us, what we're talking about, when we talk about reproductive rights and when we're talking about healthcare for the trans folks. But, in the end, the place where the rubber meets the rope is in that clinical room between a patient and a provider, and that to me is the center we should engage on."

El-Sayed argued that Republicans agree with his belief that treatment decisions should be between a patient and their doctor, pointing to the Right to Try Act, which allows terminally ill patients to try experimental drug treatments that aren't yet approved by the Food and Drug Administration after they have exhausted all other treatment options.

"Because conservatives fought for a very long time for this legislation called 'Right to Try' legislation, which is the idea that the government couldn't tell you [that] you couldn't have a certain medication," El-Sayed said.
TRUMP ADMINISTRATION PROBE COULD UPEND WIDELY USED TRANSGENDER YOUTH TREATMENT GUIDELINES

A transgender rights supporter takes part in a rally outside the U.S. Supreme Court as the justices hear arguments in a case on transgender health rights in Washington, D.C., on Dec. 4, 2024. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)

"So they agree that the decision about healthcare ought to be between the person and their provider. That's it. So let's use that standard, and keep to that standard, and make sure the government doesn't have the ability to tell you what you can or cannot do with your own life," El-Sayed said.
However, the research on the efficacy of treating individuals with gender dysphoria by allowing them to change sexes with "cross-sex" hormones and puberty blockers is limited.

The World Professional Association for Transgender Health, whose guidelines are used by leading medical associations like the American Academy of Peditatrics, is currently facing a lawsuit from the Federal Trade Commission stemming from allegations that its guidelines misled parents about the "medical consensus and medical necessity, as well as the safety and effectiveness" of sex change procedures.

The FTC has accused WPATH of failing to disclose the side effects associated with some procedures, such as patients experiencing incontinence, erectile pain, mood disturbances, pelvic pain and vaginal pain stemming from "cross-sex" hormones.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Meanwhile, countries that have socialized medicine have put restrictions in place for minors seeking sex changes. In England, the National Health Service put a pause on "cross-sex" hormones for 16- and 17-year-olds in March after finding research was "really weak" to support it.
The country already had a ban in place restricting children under 16 years old from taking sex-change hormones.
El-Sayed campaign spokesperson Roxie Richner said the Senate candidate has impeccable medical credentials.

"Dr. El-Sayed earned a medical doctorate from Columbia University and a doctorate in public health from Oxford University," she said. "That’s two doctorates—he has earned the right to be called "doctor" twice over. He has spent his career improving healthcare for Michiganders through innovative public health programs, including the elimination of millions of dollars in medical debt, increased access to Narcan, and the creation of a state-of-the-art air quality monitoring network."
Elaine Mallon is a writer for Fox News Digital and Fox Business covering national politics.

title: White House unloads on violent ‘criminal alien’ nabbed after investigators uncover election offense
summary: Anthony Tyrone Higgs, a Bahamian green card holder with a violent rap sheet, was arrested after officials say he illegally voted in the 2020 election.
story: Federal prosecutors charge a Honduran national with voter fraud in California after he allegedly registered to vote under an alias and cast ballots in multiple elections. Fox News' Matt Finn reports on the federal indictment details, revealing the suspect received a voter registration card using a gym membership. The case highlights ongoing debates surrounding voter identification laws.

A Bahamian national who arrived in the U.S. during President Gerald Ford’s administration and was living with a green card racked up a violent rap sheet before investigators found he voted illegally in the 2020 election, sparking the deportation process, officials say.

The case of Anthony Tyrone Higgs is only the latest in a slew of arrests connected to illegal votes cast in recent elections, as the Trump administration engages in a broader crackdown on election integrity-related crimes.

"This alien was a guest in our country who forfeited his right to be in the U.S. when he committed these violent crimes and voted in the 2020 election," White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis exclusively told Fox News Digital on Friday.
ICE ARRESTS PERUVIAN NATIONAL ACCUSED OF ILLEGALLY VOTING IN 2024 ELECTION AS DHS CITES SIMILAR CASES
ICE agents assemble in Minnesota, left; Anthony Tyrone Higgs, inset right. (Charly Triballeau/Getty Images; DHS)
"Any noncitizens who vote illegally in our elections will be arrested and removed. American elections are only for Americans."
Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), a division of DHS, confirmed in a statement that Higgs had illegally voted in the 2020 election.
FORMER KANSAS MAYOR WHO PLEADED GUILTY TO ILLEGAL VOTING TURNS HIMSELF IN TO ICE
HSI’s Atlanta office arrested Higgs in Decatur, Georgia on Sept. 3, and he is currently in the custody of ERO, the ICE subdivision that handles migrant removal operations.

Higgs was admitted into the U.S. in October 1976 as a lawful permanent resident – commonly dubbed a green card holder. The Trump DHS has since placed him in proceedings to revoke his immigration status due to his lengthy rap sheet.
TRUMP DOJ UNLEASHES LARGEST DENATURALIZATION EFFORT IN DEPARTMENT HISTORY — AND SAYS IT’S ‘ONLY THE BEGINNING’
Sen. Markwayne Mullin speaks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington, March 5, 2026. (J. Scott Applewhite/AP Photo)
"This criminal alien from the Bahamas has a rap sheet for multiple violent crimes, including armed robbery, domestic violence, and assault on a police officer," DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said.
"On top of all of that, he illegally voted in the 2020 election," he added.
MORE THAN A QUARTER-MILLION NONCITIZENS MAY BE REGISTERED TO VOTE IN 4 KEY STATES, DHS ALLEGES
A Homeland Security Investigations logo is displayed ahead of Super Bowl LIX security operations in New Orleans on Feb. 5, 2025. (Aaron M. Sprecher/Getty Images)
Higgs’ record also includes resisting arrest, two counts of grand larceny and two counts of possession of a weapon during a violent crime.
Of the voting-related charge, Mullin said just one noncitizen casting a ballot is enough to cancel out an American citizen’s vote.
"Thanks to the hard work of the men and women of ICE, this criminal will be removed from our country and can never interfere in our elections again," he continued.
DHS also provided several other recent cases of illegal immigrants or ineligible voters committing or being charged with election-related crimes.

In August, Colombian illegal immigrant Carlos Jaramillo-Grajales was sentenced to three years in prison following an ICE investigation that led to a guilty plea in a case where he was found to have committed identity theft to illegally vote in elections for more than 20 years, according to the agency.
"Federal immigration laws serve to safeguard our nation’s borders and protect the integrity of our government," said Gregory Kehoe, U.S. attorney for the Middle District of Florida.
"Those who seek to circumvent, exploit, or break these laws will be prosecuted fully," he said in an August statement.

In New Jersey, a Slovakian national was found to have illegally voted in the 2022 midterms, according to HSI – which also cited the case of an Australian national accused of illegally casting ballots in both 2022 and 2024 in Louisiana.
Mauritanian national Mahady Sacko was busted by an ICE and FBI partnership in Democrat-run Philadelphia, and charged with voter fraud.

Sacko allegedly voted illegally multiple times going back to 2008. He was already under an order of removal, DHS said in a statement, stating that he "exhausted all appeals" and an immigration board upheld his removal order as of 2002 but he remained in the country.

Returning to the case of Higgs, Mullin added in a statement: "Thanks to the hard work of the men and women of ICE, this criminal will be removed from our country and can never interfere in our elections again."
